Limits, Widths, Midpoints, and Intervals from Period Labels

Source: R/period_lower.R
period_lower.Rd

Calculate lower limits, upper limits, widths, midpoints, and intervals from period labels.

Usage

period_lower(
  labels,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

period_mid(
  labels,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

period_upper(
  labels,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

period_width(
  labels,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

period_interval(
  labels,
  interpret_single = c("lower", "upper"),
  interpret_multi = NULL,
  interpret_fail = c("error", "warn", "silent")
)

Arguments

labels

Vector of period labels.

interpret_single

How to interpret a label for a single year, such as "2020". Choices are "lower" (the default) and "upper". See below for details.

interpret_multi

How to interpret a label that refers to multiple years, such as "2020-2025". Choices are NULL (the default), "at_upper", and "below_upper". See below for details.

interpret_fail

Action if element of labels cannot be interpreted. Choices are "error" (the default), "warn", and "silent".

Value

period_interval() returns a character vector, and the other functions return a numeric vector. The result has the same length as labels. If labels has names, the result has the same names.

Details

Lower and upper limits can be used to filter on periods. See below for examples.

period_mid() assigns open periods (e.g., "2025+") honorary midpoints, which are useful for plotting. An interval that is open on the right gets a midpoint half the width of the closed period with the highest lower limit, and an interval that is open on the left gets a midpoint half the width of the closed period with the lowest upper limit.

period_interval() describes each period using interval notation. For instance, "[2020, 2025)" includes 2020 but not 2025, and "(-Inf, 2000)" has no lower limit. period_interval() is useful for checking how labels are being interpreted.

Rules for interpreting inputs

Single-year

Labels for single-year periods sometimes refer to the lower limits of periods, and sometimes refer to upper limits. For instance, the label "2020" is sometimes used to refer to the period that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2021, and is sometimes used to refer to the period that starts at midnight on 1 July 2019 and ends at midnight on 1 July 2020.

The interpret_single argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_singleRuleExample
"lower""a" -> [a,a+1)"2020" -> [2020,2021)
"upper""a" -> [a-1,a)"2020" -> [2019,2020)

Multi-year

In labels for multi-year periods, the second number is sometimes the upper limit of the period, and sometimes the upper limit minus 1. For instance, the period that starts at midnight on 1 January 2020 and ends at midnight on 1 January 2025 is sometimes labelled "2020-2025" and is sometimes labelled "2020-2024".

The interpret_multi argument can be used to distinguish between the two conventions:

interpret_multiRuleExample
"at_upper""a-b" -> [a,b)"2020-2025" -> [2020,2025)
"below_upper""a-b" -> [a,b+1)"2020-2024" -> [2020,2025)

If interpret_multi is NULL (the default), then multi-year labels are interpreted using the "at_upper" convention. If, however, the "at_upper" convention leads to intervals with widths 4, 9, 14, ..., then agetime emits a message. Supplying an explicit value for interpret_multi silences this message.

Open

A period that is open on the left has no lower limit, and a period that is open on the right has no upper limit. Labels for open periods are not affected by interpret_single or interpret_multi.

Some examples of open periods:

LabelInterval
"<2000", "before 2000", "under 2000"(-Inf,2000)
"2000 or earlier", "up to 2000"(-Inf,2001)
"2000+", "2000 or more", "2000 or later"[2000,Inf)

Labels starting with "-", such as "-2000", are not accepted.

  • cohort_interval() Cohort equivalent of period_interval()

Examples

labels <- c("2025-2030", "2020-2025", "2030-2035")
period_lower(labels)
#> [1] 2025 2020 2030
period_upper(labels)
#> [1] 2030 2025 2035
period_width(labels)
#> [1] 5 5 5
period_mid(labels)
#> [1] 2027.5 2022.5 2032.5
period_interval(labels)
#> [1] "[2025, 2030)" "[2020, 2025)" "[2030, 2035)"

## use 'period_lower()' to filter on period
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
df <- tribble(
  ~period, ~count,
  "2020-2025", 20,
  "2025-2030", 5,
  "2030-2035", 11
)
df
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   period    count
#>   <chr>     <dbl>
#> 1 2020-2025    20
#> 2 2025-2030     5
#> 3 2030-2035    11
df |> filter(period_lower(period) >= 2025)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   period    count
#>   <chr>     <dbl>
#> 1 2025-2030     5
#> 2 2030-2035    11

## midpoint of open periods
period_mid(c("2020-2030", "2030-2040", "2040+")) # 2045
#> [1] 2025 2035 2045
period_mid(c("2020-2025", "2025-2030", "2030+")) # 2032.5
#> [1] 2022.5 2027.5 2032.5

## 'interpret_single' is "lower" (the default)
period_lower("2025")
#> [1] 2025
period_upper("2025")
#> [1] 2026
period_width("2025")
#> [1] 1
period_interval("2025")
#> [1] "[2025, 2026)"

## 'interpret_single' is "upper"
period_lower("2025", interpret_single = "upper")
#> [1] 2024
period_upper("2025", interpret_single = "upper")
#> [1] 2025
period_width("2025", interpret_single = "upper")
#> [1] 1
period_interval("2025", interpret_single = "upper")
#> [1] "[2024, 2025)"

## 'interpret_multi' is "at_upper"
## (the default, NULL, behaves like "at_upper")
period_upper("2025-2030")
#> [1] 2030
period_width("2025-2030")
#> [1] 5
period_interval("2025-2030")
#> [1] "[2025, 2030)"

## 'interpret_multi' is "below_upper"
period_upper("2025-2030", interpret_multi = "below_upper")
#> [1] 2031
period_width("2025-2030", interpret_multi = "below_upper")
#> [1] 6
period_interval("2025-2030", interpret_multi = "below_upper")
#> [1] "[2025, 2031)"

## no action when 'interpret_fail' is "silent"
period_lower(
  labels = c("2000-2005", "long time ago"),
  interpret_fail = "silent"
)
#> [1] 2000   NA

## names of 'labels' are kept
periods <- c(base = "2020", forecast = "2025-2030")
period_lower(periods)
#>     base forecast 
#>     2020     2025
